subject: How determine the appropriate size of the mesh

messages.author: 755aecd854f1d1f3
messages.subject: How determine the appropriate size of the mesh
parts:
Hi,

I have been running space time binomial model using R INLA. I have realised that my models are very sensitive to the size and shape of the mesh used in the model. This is because every time I run the model with a different size and probably shape of the mesh, I am getting different results.

Is there a standard way to determine the appropriate size and shape of the mesh for the data at hand?

Thanks, Damaris

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: How determine the appropriate size of the mesh
parts:
Hi,

how is the "number of trials" defined in your problem?  If it is tied to a spatial _region_, it is likely essential to treat the data as regional data, whereas I think you are currently linking your data values to single _points_ in the mesh, which should be expected to give odd results when varying the mesh resolution (when the data are actually regional)).   When the link from the spatial model to the data is done properly, the mesh resolution should be irrelevant, as long as it is "fine enough".

/Finn
